deck.name: Curiosity Mix · Medium
deck.description: Unexpected facts across animals, inventions, language, history, science and games.

questions.prompt: Which planet takes longer to rotate once relative to the stars than to orbit the Sun?
questions.explanation: Venus's sidereal rotation takes about 243 Earth days; its orbit takes about 225.

questions.prompt: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.explanation: Two pump blood through the gills; the third supplies the rest of the body.

questions.prompt: Which mammal is known for producing cube-shaped droppings?
questions.explanation: Differences in the intestinal wall's elasticity help form the shapes.

questions.prompt: What is a shark's skeleton mainly made of?
What color is a polar bear's skin beneath its fur?
questions.explanation: The fur looks white, but the underlying skin is dark.

questions.prompt: Which of these is botanically classified as a berry?
questions.explanation: Botanical berries develop from a single ovary; everyday fruit names use different rules.

questions.prompt: Which plant family includes peanuts?
questions.explanation: Peanuts are related to beans and peas, despite the word nut in their name.

questions.prompt: What kind of plant is bamboo?
What kingdom includes ordinary mushrooms?
What is rust commonly formed from?
choices: Copper reacting with nitrogen and oil
Silver reacting with carbon and salt
Iron reacting with oxygen and water
Aluminum reacting with hydrogen and wax

questions.prompt: Which metal is liquid at ordinary room temperature?
questions.explanation: Gallium melts near 30 degrees Celsius, above an ordinary 20-25 degree room.

questions.prompt: Which mountain is tallest when measured above sea level?
questions.explanation: Measuring from a mountain's base gives a different comparison from measuring above sea level.

questions.prompt: Which canal is a sea-level waterway without navigation locks?
questions.explanation: The Panama Canal uses locks to raise and lower ships.

questions.prompt: What is the world's largest desert by area?
questions.explanation: Deserts are defined by low precipitation, not by heat or sand.

questions.prompt: Cleopatra VII lived closer in time to which event?
choices: The building of the Great Pyramid
The founding of the first Egyptian dynasty
questions.explanation: Cleopatra died in 30 BCE; the Great Pyramid dates to roughly 2560 BCE, and Apollo 11 landed in 1969.

questions.prompt: Which company began in 1889 by making playing cards?
The name LEGO comes from Danish words meaning what?
questions.explanation: The Danish phrase is leg godt.

questions.prompt: At what temperature do Celsius and Fahrenheit have the same numerical value?
questions.explanation: Substituting into F = 9C/5 + 32 gives -40 on both scales.

questions.prompt: Which chess piece can normally jump over other pieces?
How many points is Q worth in standard English-language Scrabble?
questions.explanation: Z is also worth ten points; letter values differ between language editions.

questions.prompt: Which electronic instrument is traditionally played without touching it?
questions.explanation: The performer's hands influence electromagnetic fields near its antennas.

questions.prompt: Who wrote The Divine Comedy?
Who wrote Around the World in Eighty Days?
What is Sherlock Holmes's famous London address?
Which subject was not one of the five original Nobel Prize categories?
questions.explanation: The original categories were physics, chemistry, physiology or medicine, literature and peace.

questions.prompt: Who was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize?
questions.explanation: She shared the 1903 physics prize and later won the 1911 chemistry prize.

questions.prompt: Which city is home to the Taj Mahal?
Which sugar is part of DNA's backbone?
questions.explanation: RNA contains ribose instead of deoxyribose.

questions.prompt: What number does the Roman numeral M represent?
What does deuce mean in an ordinary tennis game?
Which containers served as the earliest basketball baskets?
questions.explanation: James Naismith developed basketball in 1891.

questions.prompt: Which type of joint is the human shoulder's main joint?
Which process separates a liquid mixture using differences in boiling behavior?
Which gas makes up the largest share of Earth's dry atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of dry air.

questions.prompt: Which part of an egg contains most of its fat?
Which common musical marking means to play softly?
questions.explanation: Piano is a dynamic instruction as well as the name of an instrument.

questions.prompt: Sound waves can travel through a perfect vacuum.
questions.explanation: Ordinary sound needs a medium such as air, water or a solid.

questions.prompt: Whales are mammals rather than fish.
questions.explanation: They breathe air and nurse their young.

questions.prompt: What is pareidolia?
questions.answer: Perceiving a recognizable image or pattern in something ambiguous, such as seeing a face in a cloud.

questions.prompt: What is bioluminescence?
questions.answer: Light produced by a chemical reaction in a living organism.
